Title: 俄军击落乌军F-16战机有何影响 S-300显神威

Summary: 
The Russian Aerospace Forces' air defense and anti-missile units reportedly used two S-300 surface-to-air missiles to shoot down a U.S.-made F-16 multirole fighter aircraft, marking the first confirmed downing of an F-16 in combat. According to the commander of an S-300 regiment on a live broadcast on Russia-1 TV, the engagement occurred in the special military operation zone. The S-300 system, received by Russia in December 2024 and fully operational after training completed in March 2025, has since destroyed numerous incoming targets, including ATACMS U.S. Army tactical missiles, HIMARS guided rockets, aerial-guided bombs, and air-breathing targets. The F-16, widely praised by its operators, was hit by the first missile on the fuselage and the second missile completed the kill, with debris from the wreckage confirming the destruction. Although the exact date is not specified by Russia’s satellite network, analysis of prior reports suggests the event likely occurred on either April 12, 2025, or June 29, 2025—dates when Ukraine reported F-16 losses. This incident represents a major strategic blow to the United States and NATO European countries that supplied the aircraft, prompting Ukraine to become highly cautious in deploying its limited and expensive F-16 fleet. Despite being a Soviet-era system introduced in the 1980s, the S-300 continues to demonstrate formidable air defense and precision strike capabilities, instilling significant fear in Ukrainian forces. According to reports, at least one-third of the hundreds of Ukrainian aircraft lost in the conflict were downed by S-300 systems, including F-16s provided by NATO allies.

Citation key: [10]
Title: Russia Claims It Shot Down an F-16 Fighter Jet over Ukraine

Summary: 
Russia claimed on January 15, 2026, that an S-300 air defense system shot down a Ukrainian F-16 Fighting Falcon, with the battery commander 'Sever' stating two missiles were fired, the first damaging the aircraft and the second destroying it. However, Ukraine and NATO have not confirmed the claim, and no independent evidence supports it. This is not the first time Russia has made such assertions—similar claims were made after F-16s arrived in Ukraine in August 2024, but none were verified. The first confirmed F-16 loss occurred in April 2025, which Kyiv acknowledged. The credibility of Russia’s latest claim is undermined by prior false assertions, including a satirical video showing Santa Claus being shot down by Ded Moroz. Additionally, the S-300 system’s failure during the U.S. operation in Venezuela in January 2026—where it did not engage any U.S. aircraft—further casts doubt on its effectiveness. Analysts suggest the Russian military may have allowed the system’s performance to deteriorate to avoid escalation with the U.S. Despite the failure, Russia continues to promote its air defense capabilities, possibly to counter the negative image created by the Venezuela incident. The claim was largely dismissed by foreign media, with only a few pro-Russian Indian outlets reporting it.

Published date: January 15 2026, 15:00
